title: SLO experimentation decision log and triage automation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a decision-log + automated triage pipeline for SLO experiments so that product and infra teams can run controlled SLO relaxations/tightenings, capture rationale, and trigger automated rollout/rollback gates. This ticket covers the PM scope: synthesis of decision heuristics, acceptance criteria, UI hooks for the Console runbook, and integration points with ENG automation for rollouts and playbook steps.

Motivation: We run frequent SLO experiments (quantization, batching, new kernel families, autoscaling policies) and currently track outcomes in ad-hoc docs. Engineers lack a repeatable way to: (1) record the decision rationale and hypothesis, (2) map experiments to OKRs and error-budget tranches, (3) auto-trigger partial rollbacks when burn-rate thresholds are crossed. This creates operational risk and slows iteration.

Scope and deliverables:
- PM artifact: canonical Decision Log template (Confluence) + mapping to initiative/OKR.
- Console UX: an Experiment card in the Initiative Tracker that displays decision-state, linked PRs, and an automated rollback toggle.
- Automation contract: alert -> triage playbook mapping used by ENG to wire rollbacks (slo-burn-rate > X for Y minutes).
- Acceptance criteria and runbook snippets for on-call.

Non-goals: full implementation of rollback automation across all regions (ENG will scope incremental rollout). Not covering billing or quota changes in this ticket.

Related artifacts and references:
- PRD (WIP): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/SLO+Experimentation+Decision+Log
- Example incident notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/replay-2025-11-slo-burn.pdf
- Console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/slo-experiments/2026-02-mockups.png
- GitHub proposal for automation contract: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-proposals/pull/87
- Existing initiative context: PM-40217 (Reliability Initiative Hub)

Stakeholders:
- PM: Sofia Martinez (assignee)
- Eng: Cliff Huang (runtime), Priya Nair (observability)
- Design: Raoul Vega (Console)
- SRE/Oncall: Maya Patel

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative gating vs. fast experimentation: we recommend a two-tier gate (soft-alpha with elevated monitoring + strict rollback for production-facing experiments).
- Manual decision log entry vs. automated inference: initial rollout relies on a structured manual template to ensure quality of rationale; future phases will pre-fill fields from PR metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision Log template published and linked from Initiative Tracker.
- Console displays experiment states (Draft / Running / Observed / Rolled-back / Promoted).
- Automation contract doc accepted by ENG and an initial PoC that can trigger a canary rollback based on slo-burn-rate (> 4x baseline sustained for 10m).
- At least two pilot experiments (runtime batching tweak, kernel selection change) executed using the flow with postmortem entries.

Metrics of success:
- Reduction in time-to-decision for SLO experiments from avg 6 days -> <= 3 days.
- Reduction in mean time to rollback for regressions from avg 90m -> <= 20m for covered experiments.
- Clear linkage between experiments and OKRs for quarter planning (manual audit sample >= 90%).

risks: False positives in slo-burn-rate detection could cause unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by two-step gate and manual review for production experiments.
Incomplete telemetry for some legacy routes — we will block promotion until instrumentation reaches coverage threshold.
Owner churn for pilots could delay postmortems — require clear handoff and calendar blockers.
